title: Unveiling the potential: A systematic review of ChatGPT in transforming mathematics teaching and learning
venue: EURASIA Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the broader question of how ChatGPT is being used in mathematics education and what benefits and drawbacks have been reported in the emerging literature. The authors conducted a systematic review to synthesize empirical and conceptual studies on ChatGPT’s role in mathematics teaching and learning, with attention to implications for student learning, engagement, teacher support, and instructional practice.

The intervention or approach under review is the use of ChatGPT as a generative AI tool in mathematics education, including lesson planning, question answering, personalized feedback, problem-solving assistance, and support for student engagement. The review used Google Scholar and PRISMA methods, ultimately synthesizing 31 studies spanning exploratory, descriptive, comparative, experimental, qualitative, mixed-methods, and review-style designs. The included studies covered a range of educational levels, but the paper does not isolate a single population or controlled intervention cohort.

Across the reviewed studies, ChatGPT was generally found to offer useful support for lesson preparation, personalized learning, student motivation, and immediate feedback, while also showing clear limitations in handling complex mathematical reasoning, spatial geometry, derivatives, and other difficult topics. The review concludes that ChatGPT can complement mathematics instruction, but should be integrated carefully and in balance with human teacher guidance because of accuracy concerns, over-reliance risks, and ethical issues such as plagiarism and privacy.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review, but it synthesizes heterogeneous primarily descriptive, exploratory, and small empirical studies rather than a single rigorous experimental design. The review does not report a meta-analytic effect size and relies on thematic synthesis, so causal credibility is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The review suggests potentially meaningful benefits for mathematics learning, motivation, and teacher support, but the evidence base is inconsistent and often context-specific. Reported gains are promising yet not robustly quantified across studies, so the overall impact remains modest and uncertain.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of ChatGPT use in mathematics teaching and learning, including lesson planning support, student Q&A, personalized responses, and problem-solving assistance.

finding.finding_summary: Across the 31 studies synthesized, ChatGPT showed promise for supporting mathematical problem-solving and exam performance, but results varied by difficulty and topic. Reported findings included 90% overall accuracy on middle-school exam questions in one study, 83% accuracy on low-difficulty national exam items, but only 10% accuracy on higher-difficulty items; it also struggled with derivatives, spatial geometry, and complex equations.
finding.measure: Mathematics problem-solving accuracy, exam-question accuracy, and performance on word problems/national exam items

finding.finding_summary: The review reports repeated evidence that ChatGPT can increase student motivation, interest, confidence, and engagement in mathematics learning. One included study reported learning interest at 80.33%, and other studies described improved self-efficacy and more engaging, dynamic learning experiences.
finding.measure: Learning interest, motivation, engagement, self-efficacy, and attitude surveys/qualitative reports

finding.finding_summary: Several included studies suggest ChatGPT can support problem-solving, critical thinking, and mathematical thinking, especially when used interactively. However, other studies found that heavy reliance on ChatGPT could weaken skill development, and ChatGPT often produced incorrect solutions or weaker strategies than human teachers for some tasks.
finding.measure: Problem-solving quality, mathematical thinking, and critical-thinking-related task performance

finding.finding_summary: The review indicates that ChatGPT can help teachers with lesson planning, student support, assessment generation, and answering questions, thereby improving instructional efficiency. Included studies also noted quick generation of written materials and diversified responses that may reduce teacher time demands, although some outputs required substantial checking or correction.
finding.measure: Teacher lesson-planning support, assessment generation, response generation speed, and task automation
